releases.title: Users pie matches official spend
highlights: The Users list Cursor vs other pie now adds up to the official Spent total.
Opening a person scales that pie to their official spend, using the same mix.
User bars and Cursor-model sort still use matched events.

releases.title: Overview pie matches official spend
highlights: Cursor vs other on Overview now adds up to the official Spent total.
The split still comes from aggregated models, then recent events if models are missing.
Users-tab mix is unchanged and still uses matched events.

releases.title: Overview shows Cursor vs other beside the budget
highlights: Overview places the Cursor vs other pie next to the budget usage card.
The mix uses the same Cursor / other colors as Users.
Spend, remaining, and people tiles stay on the budget card.

releases.title: Cursor-model sort uses each user’s mix
highlights: Users → Cursor models ranks people by how much of their own spend is Cursor models.
Someone mostly on Cursor now ranks above a heavier spender who is mostly other models.
People with no model events stay at the bottom of that sort.

releases.title: User bars show Cursor vs other spend
highlights: Each user usage bar stays the same length, split into Cursor models and other models.
The Users list can sort by Cursor model usage.
Totals and cap percent on each row stay the same.

releases.title: Slim menu and an in-app Settings page
highlights: The menu bar dropdown keeps Open, Settings, Refresh, and Quit.
View, theme, refresh interval, and Dock badge live on the Settings tab.
Account and version details moved out of the dropdown into Settings.

releases.title: Current-month daily spend and 7-day top spenders
highlights: Overview spend is the current calendar month, with one bar per day.
Spend spikes lists the three people who spent the most in the last 7 days.
The graph no longer reads as a cycle total; peak is the busiest day.

releases.title: Per-user models load outside the newest event window
highlights: User details fetch that person's events when the team-wide page window missed them.
Top 3 models and Cursor vs other no longer stay empty for older high spenders.
Matched events already in the snapshot are still used without an extra request.

releases.title: Usage loads when api2.cursor.sh is unreachable
highlights: Model spend, events, and plan info fall back to cursor.com dashboard APIs.
The window still fills when api2.cursor.sh does not resolve.
Cookie-backed dashboard calls stay read-only and never persist tokens.
The menu and window show the installed version so you can tell which build is running.
Only Cursor admins can open usage data; other roles see a permission message.

releases.title: Month graph, user mix, and mission-control window
highlights: Spend this cycle pages usage events from the first of the month.
Users pie falls back to aggregated model spend when events do not match.
User details match Cursor owningUser events for top models and graphs.

releases.title: Spend graph covers the whole month
highlights: Usage events are requested from the first of the month with string dates Cursor accepts.
The app pages through events instead of keeping only the newest thousand.
Spend this cycle can show days before today, not a single spike.

releases.title: Cursor vs other pie uses model totals
highlights: The Users pie uses aggregated model spend when events do not match a person.
Group views no longer show $0.00 for Cursor vs other.
Matched per-user events still win when they are available.

releases.title: User top models now match real Cursor events
highlights: User details read owningUser from Cursor usage events.
Top 3 models, the pie, and the spend graph now attach to the right person.
Event IDs are no longer mistaken for user IDs.

releases.title: Month graph, top models, and Cursor vs other pie
highlights: Spend this cycle starts on the first day of the month.
User details show the three most-used models.
A pie chart on Users and user details shows Cursor models vs other models.

releases.title: Mission-control UI, new icon, gauges and graphs
highlights: New app icon and a darker ink-and-cyan look with avatars, SF Symbols, and cards.
Overview opens on a usage gauge, spend tiles, and an area graph for the cycle.
Users and models are card rows — click a person for their graph and model mix.
Usage sort is percent of cap. The filter keeps what you type.

releases.title: One window, tabs, graph, and spend spikes
highlights: Open Cursor Usage is a single window with Overview, Models, and Users tabs.
Dark mode toggle, plus filter and sort on models and users.
Overview includes a usage graph for this billing cycle.
Users who spend unusually fast in 6–24 hours are marked as spikes.
Click a user to see their spend graph, models, tokens, and recent usage.

releases.title: Global budget and model filters
highlights: View → Global shows the enterprise-wide budget from Cursor’s usage summary.
Model Breakdown can filter All models, Cursor models, or Other models.
Cursor models are Grok 4.5 / 4.6 and Composer. Auto keeps only the children that match.
Filtered spend and percent still use the same budget number.
Leaving Enter Group ID empty now opens Global.

releases.title: Users by Usage sort, restored
highlights: Users by Usage again has Usage / Name / Cap and Desc / Asc sort popups.
Each user’s percent is against their personal cap, not the group total.

releases.title: Public download page
highlights: First public installer on GitHub Releases.
Every package build now bumps the version automatically.
Download page at doron-n.github.io/cursor-usage-menubar.
